name: Salthollow
_identity: SALTHOLLOW. Pop. ~400, no Kin Hall, and no ambition to have one. Salt wind off Tideglass comes up the coast, hits Eastwind Ridge and drops here; salt air and still air together is what cures a hide, so there has been a tanyard on this shoulder for four hundred years and a village round it for three hundred and eighty. It lives off the tanyard, the change paddock where drovers swap a tired team before the climb, and a provisioner with more stock than a village this size can explain -- because everything on this coast comes past the door.
_plan: Two streets and a green. The ridge road comes in west and the coast road leaves south, and they cross on the green rather than at a junction, so the middle of the village is a place rather than a corner. THE EAST ROAD IS SHUT and has been for thirty-one years: that rockfall is the load-bearing fact of the whole act, because it is why forty crates of Foundation equipment and a twelve-ton crane in six pieces have to go over a ridge instead of along a beach. THE LONG TABLE is what the player is meant to remember: one elm table on the green where anybody off the road eats free in exchange for telling the table what they saw, which is how a village that cannot see round the corner buys its warnings. This season every single person sitting at it has seen a dray, and somebody has pinned a printed Foundation haulage notice down the middle of the carving.

text: SALTHOLLOW TANYARD. Four hundred years, and the wind has never once turned.
Hides from the drove road, cured in salt air that has come up off Tideglass.
Nowhere else on this coast is both salt enough and still enough. Hence a village.
KIN CLINIC - open all night, every night, because the road is.
Beds for drovers on one side and the other kind of bed on the other.
PROVISIONER - the largest stock between Stonewake and the water,
and every bit of it has come over the ridge on somebody's back.
THE BEACON WATCH. Wood store, ladder, oil, and the rota on the door.
Salthollow has kept the light on Eastwind Ridge since before there was a Salthollow.
Nine names on the rota. Every one of them has done it in the dark, alone, in a gale.
THE LONG TABLE. Sit down. Eat. Nobody will ask you for anything but the news.
That is the arrangement, and it is four hundred years old, and it is not a charity:
a village on a road that cannot see round the corner buys its warnings a plate at a time.
The table itself, one piece of elm, and every inch of it carved with names.
Somebody has pinned a printed notice down the middle of it, over the carving.
FOUNDATION HAULAGE - RIDGE ROAD - PRIORITY OF PASSAGE. It is signed. It is polite.
EAST ROAD CLOSED. The stone came down in one night thirty-one years ago.
The flat road. The shore road. The one that goes to Tideglass without a hill on it.
Everything that moves on this coast has gone over the ridge ever since.
STILLWATER CONCORD - COAST SURVEY OFFICE
Open. Understaffed. A hand-written card in the window: WE STILL TAKE REPORTS.
THE CHANGE PADDOCK. Rest your stock. Water is free and the hay is not.
A team that goes up the ridge tired does not come down it at all.
ROUTE 4 SOUTH - TIDEGLASS. Down off the shoulder, and then it is flat and it is sand.
You will see the water a long time before you get to it. Everyone says that. It is true.
The road bell, on its post, with a rope worn shiny.
Rung for a fire, for a wreck, and for the beacon needing wood.
It has been rung four times this year and three of them were for the beacon.
